A1.justification: Both complete, readable 14-page PDFs describe the same DAS study. The text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original DAS evaluations on peer reviews, blogs, emails, and research papers, including a nine-participant study with 25 test cases.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the participant study, benchmark evaluations, ablations, and appendix research-paper experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same CoSENT filtering, tournament elimination, dynamic weighting, and aggregation across trials. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ICLR reviews, Blog Authorship Corpus, Enron emails, and research-paper data. The one-to-many and whole-corpus test scenarios are unchanged, including Appendix B.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: random guessing in Table 2, AIDBench in Tables 3, 4, and 8, and DAS-PE in Table 5. The new acknowledgement of AIDBench contributors introduces no comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same metrics, model choices, candidate settings, and evaluation procedures. The participant study remains nine participants and 25 test cases.

E4.justification: The progressive-elimination ablation in Table 5, model comparisons in Table 11, and rank-progression analysis in Appendix D.1/Figure 4 are unchanged. Their relocation introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: The descriptions of five independent trials and randomized candidate ordering are unchanged. No seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing is added or removed.

E6.justification: All result entries and figure content are retained. For example, Tables 2, 6, and 9 still report Rank@20 of 44% for reviews, 94% for blogs, 88% for emails, and 92% for research papers.

T1.justification: The formal problem definition, weighting equation, and hypergeometric random-baseline derivation remain unchanged in Equations 1–6. Appendix C moves without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable authorship matching, privacy risks, and benchmark advantages.

C2.justification: The interpretations of performance and privacy implications remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning model coverage and prompt design, and the appendix mechanism explanations are preserved.

D1.justification: Implementation parameters, hardware, cost and runtime disclosures, the prompt template, and appendix data-processing and platform details are unchanged. The new acknowledgements provide no additional technical or access instructions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged after matching references across page breaks. Thanking AIDBench contributors does not revise the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgement section before the references on page 9, thanking anonymous volunteers, Zichen Wen, Dadi Guo, and funding organizations. The existing research prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement causes reference and appendix reflow. Figure 3 shifts columns, Table 7 moves from page 11 to 12, and Figure 4 moves from page 13 to 14; their content and dimensions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds contributor credit and funding disclosure, but leaves the methods, evidence, results, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged. The accompanying layout shifts do not materially affect readability, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
